profile.reading:
This building is SLC3, one of five data centers DataBank operates on its Granite Point Campus in Bluffdale, Utah, roughly 20 miles south of Salt Lake City. DataBank's own campus page places SLC3 at 14926 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, with 55,780 square feet of IT space and 7 megawatts of critical IT load, built to a 2N power and N+1 cooling design. A third-party aggregator separately describes SLC3 as "built to Tier III design standards" with 6.3 megawatts of power; DataBank's own page does not use Tier language and states 7 megawatts, so the aggregator's figures are noted here as unconfirmed secondary claims rather than adopted as fact. DataBank acquired the underlying Granite Point site from C7 Data Centers in 2017. Across the full five-building campus, DataBank states a combined 257,770 square feet of IT space and roughly 45.9 megawatts of critical IT load on about 23 acres, fed by diverse A and B power feeds from Rocky Mountain Power in an N+1 substation configuration, with FISMA, SSAE 18, HIPAA/HITECH, PCI, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications applicable campus-wide. DataBank does not publish a specific year-opened date for SLC3 on its current site. Utah's "Silicon Slopes" technology corridor has grown substantially around Salt Lake and Utah counties over the past decade, drawing data center, software, and financial-technology employers, and Bluffdale's industrial-zoned land along the Pony Express Road corridor has become a recognized data center cluster anchored by DataBank's campus alongside other operators in the immediate area.

Rocky Mountain Power filed for what it described as Utah's first major large-load energy agreement under the state's 2025 large-load legislation in early February 2026, an "Operation Gigawatt" filing with the Utah Public Service Commission covering a data center customer that agreed to cover its own service costs; this filing does not name DataBank or the Granite Point campus specifically, so it is noted here only as regional grid-planning context, not as a confirmed connection to SLC3. Utah's broader "Silicon Slopes" branding effort has helped position the state as a lower-cost alternative to coastal data center markets for operators seeking reliable power and a business-friendly regulatory climate.

DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Granite Point Campus SLC3, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 14926 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065, and states 7 MW of critical IT load and 55,780 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC3 in Bluffdale, Utah publishes 7 MW of IT capacity across 55,780 square feet of technical space, placing it third among the three Utah facilities that report a megawatt figure.

The facility's physical footprint of roughly 8 square feet per kilowatt suggests a mixed-use colocation design rather than a purpose-built high-density training shell. At standard colocation density of 10 kW per rack, 7 MW supports approximately 700 racks. At the 40 kW per rack typical of AI training hardware, the same power supports roughly 175 racks. The operator's published specifications do not include redundancy tier ratings, connectivity details, or compliance certifications, limiting what can be inferred about the facility's suitability for any particular workload class.

Utah's known IT capacity totals 39 MW across just three facilities that publish figures. SLC3's 7 MW represents 18 percent of that reported total. However, the majority of mapped Utah data centers publish no capacity data, so actual installed base in the state is substantially larger and SLC3's real share is proportionally smaller. For AI workload planning, 7 MW is modest capacity. It suffices for inference or small training runs but sits far below the scale of purpose-built hyperscale facilities that now anchor large model training programs.
